---
title: Testing reference
description: How tests are defined and run in Oxygen
type: reference
---

Tests live in their own `.test.yml` files. Each file points at one agent
(its **target**), lists a set of **cases** — a prompt plus the answer you
expect — and says how many times to run each one. An LLM judge scores every
run against the expected answer.

<Note>
Only `.agentic.yml` agents can be tested. Inline `tests:` blocks in
`.agent.yml` or `.workflow.yml` files are no longer supported — `.test.yml` is
the only way to define tests.
</Note>

## Test file format

```yaml sales.agentic.test.yml
target: sales.agentic.yml   # optional — inferred from the filename

settings:
  concurrency: 5            # runs executed in parallel
  runs: 3                   # times to run each case
  judge_model: gpt-5-mini   # model that scores each run

cases:
  - name: signups-last-month
    prompt: "How many users signed up last month?"
    expected: "1,247 new user signups"
    tags: [users, critical]

  - prompt: "Show me top 5 customers by lifetime value"
    expected: |
      A ranked list of 5 customers ordered by total spend,
      including customer names and their LTV amounts.
    tags: [customers]
```

### Top-level fields

| Field      | Type   | Default                | Description |
| ---------- | ------ | ---------------------- | ----------- |
| `target`   | string | inferred from filename | Path to the `.agentic.yml` agent under test. If omitted, `sales.agentic.test.yml` targets `sales.agentic.yml` in the same directory. |
| `name`     | string | —                      | Optional display name for the test file. |
| `settings` | object | see below              | Run settings. |
| `cases`    | list   | required               | The test cases. |

### `settings`

| Field         | Type    | Default | Description |
| ------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `runs`        | integer | `3`     | Number of times each case is run. Consistency is measured as agreement across these runs. |
| `concurrency` | integer | `5`     | How many runs execute in parallel. |
| `judge_model` | string  | —       | Model used as the LLM judge. Prefer a different model family than the agent's to avoid self-preference bias. |

### `cases`

| Field      | Type            | Default  | Description |
| ---------- | --------------- | -------- | ----------- |
| `prompt`   | string          | required | The question sent to the agent. |
| `expected` | string          | required | The expected answer. The judge checks each run's answer for factual consistency with it. |
| `name`     | string          | —        | Stable label for the case, used by `--case` and shown in progress output instead of the prompt. |
| `tags`     | list of strings | `[]`     | Tags for filtering with `--tag`. |
| `tool`     | string          | —        | Accepted by the schema, but tool-use assertions are not enforced yet — setting it has no effect on pass/fail. |

## How evaluation works

For each case, Oxygen:

1. Runs the target agent `runs` times with the case's `prompt`
2. Asks the judge model whether each answer is factually consistent with
   `expected` — formatting and wording differences are ignored
3. Records a pass rate per case, and whether all runs reached the same verdict

Across the file, the **score** is the overall pass rate over every case and
run, and **consistency** is the fraction of cases whose runs all agreed.

## Running tests

Tests run on your Oxygen deployment with `oxyc`, the Oxygen API client. Install
it with `npm i -g @oxy-hq/cli` and sign in with `oxyc login`. The deployment
queues the eval and runs it against the test files and agents the workspace
has **compiled** — what you pushed, not the files on your machine — so push a
new or edited `.test.yml` (and the agent change it tests) before you run it.
The file argument is the test file's path in the workspace, from the project
root.

```sh
# Run every compiled .test.yml file; waits for the run and prints a summary
oxyc evals run --workspace <workspace-id>

# Run one file
oxyc evals run sales.agentic.test.yml --workspace <workspace-id>

# Only cases tagged "critical"
oxyc evals run --workspace <workspace-id> --tag critical

# One case, by 0-based index, name, or exact prompt
oxyc evals run sales.agentic.test.yml --workspace <workspace-id> --case signups-last-month
```

### Accuracy thresholds

Use `--min-accuracy` to fail the command (exit code 9) when the score is below
a threshold — useful as a CI quality gate:

```sh
oxyc evals run --workspace <workspace-id> --min-accuracy 0.8
```

Each test file produces one score. When several files run,
`--threshold-mode` controls how the threshold is applied: `average` (default)
checks the average score across files; `all` requires every file's score to
meet it.

```sh
oxyc evals run --workspace <workspace-id> --min-accuracy 0.8 --threshold-mode all
```

### Machine-readable output

The summary shows each file's score and the prompts of the runs that failed.
`--json` prints the full results as JSON on stdout instead. `--output-json`
also writes the JSON to a file at the test file's path
(`sales.agentic.test.results.json`, or `test-results.json` when running every
file), or to the file you name after it.

```sh
oxyc evals run sales.agentic.test.yml --workspace <workspace-id> --json
```

### Long runs

`--detach` queues the run and prints its id; `oxyc evals wait <run-id>` picks
it up later. `--wait <seconds>` stops waiting after that long (exit code 7)
while the run goes on.

## CLI reference

```sh
oxyc evals run [FILE] --workspace <workspace-id> [OPTIONS]
oxyc evals wait <RUN_ID> --workspace <workspace-id> [OPTIONS]
```

- `FILE` — the workspace path of a `.test.yml` file. Omit it to run every
  compiled `.test.yml` file in the workspace.

| Flag                         | Description | Default |
| ---------------------------- | ----------- | ------- |
| `--workspace <id>`           | The workspace to run in (required) | — |
| `--tag <tag>`                | Only run cases with this tag | — |
| `--case <case>`              | Only run one case, by 0-based index, `name`, or exact prompt. Requires `FILE` | — |
| `--regrade <file>`           | Grade the answers recorded in a results file again, without running the agent. Requires `FILE` | — |
| `--json`                     | Print the full results as JSON instead of the summary | `false` |
| `--output-json [file]`       | Also write the full JSON results to a file | — |
| `--min-accuracy <threshold>` | Minimum score (0.0–1.0). Exit code 9 if below | — |
| `--threshold-mode <mode>`    | `average` or `all` | `average` |
| `--wait [seconds]`           | Stop waiting after this many seconds (exit code 7); the run goes on | wait to the end |
| `--detach`                   | Queue the run, print its id, and return (`run` only) | `false` |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --------- | ------- |
| `0` | The run finished, and met `--min-accuracy` if one was given |
| `1` | The run failed, was cancelled, or timed out |
| `4` | Not signed in, or not a member of the workspace |
| `5` | No such workspace, or the test file is not in the compiled workspace (push it) |
| `6` | The test file does not parse, or `--case` matched nothing |
| `7` | Retryable: the deployment could not read the compiled workspace, or `--wait <seconds>` ran out |
| `9` | Accuracy below `--min-accuracy` |

## CI example

The tests score the workspace's compiled revision, not a pull request's
branch, so run them after a push to the branch the workspace serves has
compiled. Store a personal access token as a repository secret:

```yaml
- name: Run agent tests
  env:
    OXY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OXY_TOKEN }}
  run: npx @oxy-hq/cli evals run --workspace ${{ vars.OXY_WORKSPACE_ID }} --min-accuracy 0.8
```

## Error handling

- **Wrong file type** — `oxyc evals run` rejects any file that doesn't end in
  `.test.yml`, and the eval engine any test whose target isn't an
  `.agentic.yml` agent.
- **No tests found** — running `oxyc evals run` with no file fails (exit code
  5) if the workspace has no compiled `.test.yml` files.
- **Threshold failures** — the command exits with code 9 only when
  `--min-accuracy` is set and not met. If no score was produced, it prints a
  warning and exits 0.
